# BANNED DISPLAY VOCABULARY — epic-17 wave-06 slice S1 (spec AC-6).
#
# One list, two lints. tests/voice-contract.test.sh used to read it to check the four
# shipped command files (that suite was deleted in an earlier purge, commit b959b5e, and
# nothing replaced its arm); the script-output lint (slice S4) reads it to check every line
# setup.sh/doctor.sh/remove.sh print. The ownership table names "one list file under
# tests/" precisely so the two lints cannot drift to two opinions about what is internal.
#
# WHAT BELONGS HERE: vocabulary that exists only inside bionic's own machinery — the old
# dependency-lane codes, script-internal function-name prefixes, and shell mechanism words
# a user has no reason to meet. Chris, 2026-08-20: "This concept of 'lane' and in
# particular references to '3b' are very confusing. Why are we exposing this to the user?"
#
# WHAT DOES NOT: ordinary product words that happen to name a bionic feature (hooks,
# skills, agents, tiers), and the fix half of a real error message. The contract is loud on
# real errors; it is silent about how the machine works when nothing is wrong.
#
# FORMAT — consumers must honour it:
#   * one token per line;
#   * a line whose first non-blank character is `#` is a comment;
#   * blank lines are ignored;
#   * matching is case-insensitive SUBSTRING matching, so `lane` also catches `lanes`
#     and `Lane`. Add a token only when no legitimate product word contains it.
#
# The voice block itself quotes several of these tokens (it is the text that BANS them),
# so both lints exempt the block's own body — tests/voice-contract.test.sh used to be the
# second lint's home; it was deleted in an earlier purge (commit b959b5e).

lane
3a
3b
lane-3a
lane-3b
_setup_
_rm_
_doctor_
detect_
stdin
non-interactive
pipefail

# ROSTER FOOTPRINT cited the design ledger by letter-number on a printed line (epic-17 W6
# S9a, walk finding W-3). A design-doc pointer is provenance for a reader of the SOURCE; on
# a user's terminal it is a reference into a document they do not have.
design-ledger

# REMOVAL-POLICY AND RUNTIME-MODE VALUES reached the terminal (epic-17 W6 S10, six-axis
# review R-1). `keep-shared` is a column value in deps.sh's dependency table and printed
# nine times in a row on a full teardown; `mode: payload` was the remove transcript's
# second line. Both are the script naming its own internals at a user who has no way to
# know them — the same class as `lane 3b`, one list entry away from being caught. The
# other two policy values are listed with them so the class cannot come back through a
# row that has not printed yet.
keep-shared
remove-on-consent
native-uninstall-offer
mode: payload

# LIBRARY FUNCTION-NAME PREFIXES. The three payload scripts already had theirs on this
# list (`_setup_`, `_rm_`, `_doctor_`, `detect_`); the libraries beneath them did not, so
# `_dep_` and `_jit_` could reach a terminal through any line the scripts
# print. `_detect_` needs no entry — `detect_` already catches it as a substring.
# tests/script-vocabulary.test.sh used to derive the roster from payload/scripts/lib/*.sh, so a
# new library prefix arrived here deliberately rather than by somebody noticing; that suite
# was deleted in an earlier purge (commit b959b5e) and nothing replaced the derivation check.
_dep_
_jit_
# `env_` (epic-17 W7 S4, spec R4) covers the new settings-environment library both ways: its
# internal prefix `_env_` and its public `env_get`/`env_set`/`env_unset`/`env_live`, exactly
# as `detect_` covers `_detect_` and detect.sh's public probes. `environment` is a product
# word and carries no underscore, so it is untouched by this token.
env_

# HOOK FILE NAMES — AC-6's own words, and until epic-17 W6 S11 the list held no file name
# of any kind, so that clause of the criterion was green by absence rather than by
# measurement (critic F-6). These are the basenames bionic ships under payload/hooks/. A
# user told that something is wrong needs to know which capability stopped, not which
# script implements it.
#
# THIS IS NOT A BAN ON PATHS (plan A-6.3's ruling). A shipped file path printed as an
# ADDRESS the reader is being pointed at — doctor's "the constraint column is the table in
# scripts/lib/deps.sh", or "every hooks.json command resolves to a file on disk" — is
# product information a person can act on. Neither line contains a hook basename, so the
# ruling needs no exemption in the lint to hold; tests/script-vocabulary.test.sh used to
# measure that it still does — that suite was deleted in an earlier purge (commit b959b5e)
# and nothing replaced the measurement.
agent-context-guard.sh
canonical-sdlc-evidence-gate.sh
canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
context-spend.sh
dispatch-preflight.sh
execution-recorder.sh
farm-out-reminder.sh
landing-gate.sh
preflight-probe.sh
protect-database.sh
protect-main.sh
session-poker.sh
session-sweeper.sh
stop-check.sh
stop-guard.sh
stop-orders.sh
